output.brief: The VA-220 failures are coming from Pellacott's 2026-built valves, and the leak-test certificates for them appear to be fabricated. The calibration contractor found the only rig that could test VA-220s out of service since 9 January 2026, with no VA-220 test program on any other rig. Certificate tables repeat the same four sequences, some dating from before the rig failed. Your quality lab's helium retest of never-installed stock found 11% of Pellacott 2026 valves leaking at the seat, against 0–1% for older Pellacott stock and for Durrant-Hale. Claim rates on Pellacott 2026 valves are about the same for new and legacy installers and for firmware 4.1 and 4.2, so neither installers nor firmware explain the rise. Pellacott's score rose because the scoring formula rewards complete paperwork, not verified tests. I'm fairly confident (about 85–90%). Next steps: do not release the six held lots on fresh certificates. Quarantine 2026-built Pellacott stock, suspend dock-to-stock, and release only after Brenmoor's own helium testing, using Durrant-Hale to cover supply. Drop the installer remediation and chargebacks. Require rig logs or witnessed tests in scoring, and check other suppliers' records. Whether the seal change or Line 3 is the cause is still unresolved, so don't order a seal reversion yet.
